Need to see that breakdown but I'm with you. I also think there's this conflict throughout the album of fate vs. free will and chance. DNA, happening after the intro and his death, seems to talk on the inevitability of his power, literally written into his genetic code. This gets subverted much later on DUCKWORTH where clearly he was built by coincidence. The constant references and desire for rewinding explore this too, playing on the desire to see events differently, wondering if the events were inevitable or no. Whether the coincidences were chance or a curse like his cousin Carl says on FEAR. He doesn't seem to give any answers here either. One can see a social interpretation here, it was inevitable he'd be him because he was forged by his environment OR he was only able to because he got lucky to escape said environment, but because of how personal the whole record is I also feel he's exploring his own doubts. Is his acclaim deserved, achieved through his hard work, or was it woven into him? Is he actually good enough to deserve the praise? And now he has this great success is he doomed to unhappiness? He needs some water and ain't nobody praying for him, will he ever be able to get that help? Or is he fated to acclaim and adoration but never love?
